body:
Based on the PR description, most of the changes look good. Some personal feedback from my side:

>Reverted Linear mode renaming back to RAW mode for consistent short names.
>Modes are now [RGB, HSV, RAW, HSL], displayed horizontally without an extra popup for OKHSL.

I disagree with renaming "Linear" and "OKHSL" to "RAW" and "HSL". They are not the same - what is "RAW"? and "OKHSL" is different from traditional "HSL". It's not good to sacrifice accuracy for the sake of shorter names, which may confuse users.

>Sorted intensity slider to appear after the alpha slider for consistency with other slider styles.

In my opinion, placing the intensity slider before the alpha slider is easier to use. It's inconvenient if the unchanged alpha slider is in the middle.

>Fixed regressions from previous intensity slider changes.

What other specific regressions are also fixed?

> I disagree with renaming "Linear" and "OKHSL" to "RAW" and "HSL". They are not the same - what is "RAW"? and "OKHSL" is different from traditional "HSL". It's not good to sacrifice accuracy for the sake of shorter names, which may confuse users. We’ve actually been using the name RAW for years, and I haven’t seen any confusion about it, it’s already documented, and even a quick Google search brings up the right meaning. From that perspective, I wasn’t sure if it was necessary to break compatibility for something that hasn’t caused issues. For HSL, what I did was make the naming consistent across all modes so they align horizontally and are quicker to switch between. It’s mainly about UI usability just like Aseprite, which also uses short labels like RGB / HSL. Example from Aseprite: > In my opinion, placing the intensity slider before the alpha slider is easier to use. It's inconvenient if the unchanged alpha slider is in the middle. The intensity slider uses a different style from the colored sliders. Putting it in the middle (before alpha) breaks the visual flow and makes the layout feel inconsistent. Since intensity is also a less frequently used control, I felt it was better placed after alpha, so the main color sliders stay grouped together. > What other specific regressions are also fixed? A couple of regressions were addressed along the way: - Disabling the intensity slider in `EditorSettings` couldn’t be reverted, since project metadata wasn’t updated correctly. - Updating colors in HSV shapes didn’t sync properly with HSL shapes, and vice-versa, Shown in the video in description.
* Moved the bug fixes to another PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110160

>We’ve actually been using the name RAW for years.

It is changed after the intensity PR. It used to be the same as RGB sliders, but now the sliders are linear color, so RAW is incorrect.

>Example from Aseprite:

Dose aseprite use OKHSL or standard HSL? Please note they are different and can't exchange.

> It is changed after the intensity PR. It used to be the same as RGB sliders, but now the sliders are linear color, so RAW is incorrect. After the intensity PR, disabling the intensity sliders reverts the behavior back to what was previously called RAW, where values greater than 1.0 can still be set. For that reason, calling it Linear wouldn’t really be accurate either. I decided to keep the existing RAW name, since it has been documented and consistently used for years without causing confusion. Changing the label now would break compatibility unnecessarily, especially since the feature can be disabled if not needed. There’s also a translation concern: we’d end up with three modes that stay in English (RGB, HSV, OKHSL) and only one that gets translated (Linear -> e.g. خطي), which looks inconsistent. Keeping RAW keeps all four modes aligned. > Dose aseprite use OKHSL or standard HSL? Please note they are different and can't exchange. Aseprite itself uses the short label HSL for the Hue/Saturation/Lightness sliders, regardless of the exact internal model. The goal here isn’t to expose the technical color model implementation, but to present familiar and consistent labels for users. Since what people are actually doing is adjusting hue, saturation, and lightness visually, the concise HSL name makes sense and aligns with what most artists are used to.

>After the intensity PR, disabling the intensity sliders reverts the behavior back to what was previously called RAW, where values greater than 1.0 can still be set. For that reason, calling it Linear wouldn’t really be accurate either. I decided to keep the existing RAW name, since it has been documented and consistently used for years without causing confusion.

It's not about whether the intensity slider is enabled or not, it's about color space. If you set the linear color sliders to 0.5, the actual color is 0.735, it's not raw.
- See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103583#issuecomment-2703990932

>and only one that gets translated (Linear -> e.g. خطي)

I think it's better to disable the translation of "Linear" here.

>Aseprite itself uses the short label HSL for the Hue/Saturation/Lightness sliders,

If you want to copy the values of other HSL color to OKHSL, you will find the colors are not the same, so it's better to specify the color model clearly.

I didn't even realize that Linear mode is not the same as RGB like before, Reverted the change, only disabled the translation for it since other modes doesn't have translatable names.

Other changes related to intensity slider are moved to different PRs:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110386
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110384

> only disabled the translation for it since other modes doesn't have translatable names.

That's because they aren't even words. The Linear was marked for translation in #109354.

> That's because they aren't even words. The Linear was marked for translation in #109354. If we allow translating all of them then some other languages may find a workaround for all mode names but for Arabic it's impossible to translate `RGB`, `HSV` or `OKHSL`. I will revert this change for now since I only use the editor in English, just pointing out that it will look weird for all RTL languages.

> * When switching the editor to a light theme, the "color picker type" icon in the right isn't updated: > All color picker icon types in the dropdown are also affected: > In both cases, this happens even after restarting the editor, so the issue isn't in a lack of `NOTIFICATION_THEME_CHANGED` usage. It's either the icon file having an incorrect color, or the icon being incorrectly listed in the icon conversion exclusions. Fixed, for shape menu icons, the files were using the wrong color, for the Palette menu button, i can't find why it's not using the editor theme colors, i already have added the missing overrides in EditorThemeManager and it didn't update the icons. > * Pressing Ctrl + Enter on the color text field should focus it and select all its text, so you can enter another color code or name afterwards without needing to click with the mouse. It works as expected without making any changes on fedora wayland. > * Some icons don't scale up for hiDPI displays in the editor, like the context menu icons next to the Swatches section: > As well as the "Swatches" and "Recent colors" chevrons: I don't know if they do scale or not, hard to see the difference since they use 16x16 size by default which will look pixelated even when scaled. > * The Swatches context menu icon should also have a square minimum size, so that its clickable area is always square: Fixed. > For future PRs: > * We could make the value slider slightly rounded to match the focus StyleBox Made the `picker_focus_rectangle` style have sharp corners for editor, and i think we can reuse it to override other Controls focus style that have issues with the default focus style. > * The focus outline for the color picker circle could be antialiased Enabled antialiasing for the circle shapes. > The main circle is already antialiased, although it should perhaps use a slightly wider feather to improve quality. Using the default 1.0 anti-aliasing size to avoid those artifacts. Another issue: Since the corner radius of the circle shape focus is set to 256px and we do allow changing the shape width and height, the shape appears deformed when the circle shapes are not perfect and also input doesn't work correctly.

Fixed the presets arrow colors and excluded the picker cursor icon from color conversion. The Show all options available minimum width was set to `28px` similar to other menu buttons, but it wasn't enough since the Swatches button height is greater, will need to use the buttons height instead to determine it's minimum size.

> I noticed the "revert to old color" icon gets converted when using a light theme in the editor

Fixed by adding a new editor icon since we can't exclude the `Reload` icon from color conversion.

> > Using the default 1.0 anti-aliasing size to avoid those artifacts. > > I think these artifacts are due to this issue: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/68514 that stylebox corner radius downscaling doesn't account correctly for anti-aliasing size. So styleboxes with downscaled rounded corners and anti-aliasing get these overlap artifacts.

> That's because they aren't even words. The Linear was marked for translation in #109354.

I was thinking we could use LRGB for the button text, and then add tooltips to each mode with the full names (e.g. [Linear RGB] and [Standard RGB]). This way, the button text stays consistent with the acronym style, while the tooltips provide clarity and can be translated to longer names without issues.

I'm not sure about removing the mode button completely. If we add more color modes, it will have to be re-added.
Then again, it's not needed right now, so removing it makes sense.
Why the non-colorized sliders became so fat? Old: It does not look good. Colorized sliders don't have this problem.

Applied the suggestions and rebased. Note: I didn't change the picker cursor size, I am using custom icons to test that the separation is handled for the shape and sampler only based on the half cursor size. Here's the Picker unchanged.
Note: I still have more local changes for the `ColorPicker` that are hard to applied all together, so I'm waiting until the current PRs we have that changes `color_picker.cpp` to be merged first.
The non-colorized sliders are better now, but arrows have a gap: Though not sure if it can't be left like that.

> The non-colorized sliders are better now, but arrows have a gap:

Fixed and rebased. Thank you.
Needs another rebase

> The intensity slider uses a different style from the colored sliders. Putting it in the middle (before alpha) breaks the visual flow and makes the layout feel inconsistent. Since intensity is also a less frequently used control, I felt it was better placed after alpha, so the main color sliders stay grouped together.

I understand what you're describing here: the layout is more visually pleasing by grouping the alpha slider with the other colour sliders.

I also disagree that the change should be made to the position of the intensity slider because this negatively affects usability: The intensity slider directly affects the colour defined by RGB, HSV, and HSL and has nothing to do with the alpha value. Placing the alpha slider after all of the colour-related sliders is an intentional GUI design choice that makes the alpha transparency distinct from the colour. Conversely, the intensity slider is placed beside the RGB, HSV, and HSL sliders because it directly changes the RGB, HSV, and HSL values. The original ordering was purposefully designed to favour usability and clarity of function, which I believe is more valuable than visual flow in this case.

**Edit:** one option for improving the visual flow without affecting function and usability would be to change the intensity slider to be coloured, the same as the other four sliders, without moving its position.

The new Hex icon is a nice improvement. I'm on the fence about always showing OKHSL because it's already a visually complex tool for new users...
